post.description:
Extracting [`CurrentUser`] is what makes this CSRF-protected: without it a
cross-site page could sign somebody out, which is not a disaster and is
still not something anybody else gets to do.

get.description:
The first call a portal makes, and the one that tells it whether there is a
session at all — so an empty `memberships` is a real answer rather than an
error. A person who has signed in and belongs to nothing yet is exactly who
the "create an organization" screen is for.

post.description:
Add to a group needs `manage_group`; setting labels, refreshing,
decommissioning and deleting need `manage_host`; a reboot, which opens a
proposal, needs `run_job`. Decommissioned hosts are skipped and say so,
except by `decommission` (unchanged) and `delete`, which acts on nothing
else. At most 5,000 hosts; past that the request is refused whole.

# `replaces` is not optional in the way it looks

A proposal's identity is its `dedupe_key`, which begins with the **policy
id**. So previewing an edit without saying which policy it replaces compiles
the candidate under a fresh id, every key differs, and the answer is "all of
these would open and all of those would close" — which is true of a *new*
policy and nonsense for an edit.

With `replaces`, the candidate is compiled under that policy's id and
substituted for it, and the diff is about the change rather than about the
identity. Without it, the candidate is **added** to what is already there,
which is the honest reading of previewing something that does not exist yet.

# What this deliberately does not compare against

The proposals that are actually open. Those were written by the policies in
force at some past moment, so comparing with them would fold "the policy
changed" together with "the fleet changed since" — two answers in one
number, and the editor only asked about the first. Both sides here are
evaluated now, over the same snapshot.

# No status means every status

Including one this build does not recognise. The temptation is to default an
inbox to the open ones — and a default that hides rows is a default that
makes a proposal somebody is waiting on invisible without saying so. The
portal asks for what it wants to show; the API does not decide on its behalf.

# ⚠️ Why the query is a list of pairs and not a struct

`Query<T>` deserialises with `serde_urlencoded`, which **cannot** put a
repeated key into a `Vec`. `?status=open&status=snoozed` against a
`Vec<String>` field does not collect two values — it fails, and it fails
with axum's own plain-text 400, which carries no `type` for a portal to
branch on and is a different shape from every other refusal this API makes.
That is DAWG-246's problem arriving by a second route.

`Vec<(String, String)>` is what `serde_urlencoded` does support, so the
pairs are read and interpreted here. It buys one more thing worth having:
an **unknown** parameter can be refused. `?staus=open` silently returning
everything is the same failure as an unparseable status silently returning
everything, and both are a list that is quietly not what was asked for.

`jobs`, `policy`, `groups`, `hosts`, `enrollment`, `audit`,
`integrations`, as far as your role allows.

name.description: How rules and people pick it. Unique in the organization.

label_selector.description:
Labels a host must **all** carry, with exactly these values. Absent for
a purely static group. An empty map is refused: it would match every
host.

slug.description: Optional: derived from the name when it is not given.

channel_ids.description:
`nch_…` ids. May be empty: a rule for `proposal.auto_merged` with no
channels is how auto-merges are silenced.

expires_at.description: When it stops working. Absent never expires.

labels.description: Put on every host that enrols with it.

max_uses.description: How many hosts it may enrol. Absent is unlimited.

name.description:
What it is for — "web tier", "laptop test". Shown in the list, since the
value never is again.

CreatedApiTokenBody.description: The one response that carries the value.

token.description: ⚠️ **Shown once.** `enr_…`. Only its hash is kept.

CreatedTokenBody.description: The one response that carries the value.

oneOf.description:
⚠️ Absent means a **policy auto-merge**, not an unknown person. A portal
that renders this as "somebody" would be attributing a machine decision
to a human it cannot name.

proposals_closed.description: Of those, the ones it left empty — now closed as `obsolete`.

proposals_left.description: Proposals nobody had approved that the host was taken out of.

hostname.description: What it was called, for the confirmation.

policies_naming_it.description:
Live policies whose selector names it. Not changed — they are the
operator's text — and now match nothing of it.

proposals_unlinked.description: Proposals that pointed at the group, now pointing at none.

tokens_unlinked.description: Enrollment tokens whose default group it was, now with none.

DeliveryBody.description: One delivery, as the channel's log shows it.

last_error.description: The other side's words, or ours. Never the destination.

status.description:
`pending` (being tried), `delivered`, or `failed` — every attempt
used, the dead letter. A failed one can be replayed.

showing.description:
The version this body carries, which differs from `version` when an
older one was asked for. Both are here on purpose: a portal showing
version 2 of a policy on version 5 needs to know it is looking at
history rather than at the policy.

yaml.description:
Byte for byte what somebody wrote. The compiled form is derived from it
and is not handed back — there is one source of truth for what a policy
says and it is the text.

frequency.description:
`off`, `daily` or `weekly`. Sent at 08:00 in your time zone; weekly on
Mondays.

mention_email.description:
Whether you are emailed when somebody mentions you in a comment here
(DAWG-247). On unless turned off. Absent on a `PUT` leaves it alone.

fixable.description: Whether an update available to the host reaches `fixed_version`.

fixed_version.description: The version the advisory says fixes it.

first_seen_at.description: When this installed version was first seen exposed.

fixable.description:
Whether an update available to this host reaches `fixed_version`.
`false` is the urgent case: affected, and nothing to install.

fixed_version.description: The version the advisory says fixes it.

severity.description:
Normalised, from the vendor's rating or else the worst CVSS. `null`
means nobody rated it, which is not the same as harmless.

unfixable.description: How many of `exposures` no available update fixes.

FilterBody.description:
What a rule narrows its events by. Every field optional; all given must
hold. The proposal fields do not narrow host events.

known_exploited.description:
Only proposals that fix something known to be exploited (`true`), or
only those that do not (`false`).

oneOf.description: At least this severe.

first_seen_at.description: When the earliest of those exposures was first seen.

fixable_hosts.description: Of those, the ones an available update fixes.

hosts.description: Hosts with an installed version it affects.

known_exploited.description: A CVE it lists is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities.

severity.description:
Normalised, from the vendor's rating or else the worst CVSS. `null`
means nobody rated it, which is not the same as harmless.

FrozenBody.description:
What pins a host's package sources in time, as its agent reported it
(DAWG-233).

behind.description:
Known to be behind what it is offered. `false` also when nobody can
tell.

kind.description:
`releasever` (dnf's release is fixed: Amazon Linux 2023, or
`/etc/dnf/vars/releasever`), `snapshot` (apt sources on a dated
archive snapshot), or `other` from an agent newer than this server.

latest.description: The newest release it is offered, where its agent can tell.

by_label.description: Matched by the label selector. Both may be true.

static.description: Put in the group by hand.

failed_health_checks.description: Failed health checks that halt the rollout. Zero means none do.

failed_jobs.description: Failed jobs that halt the rollout. Zero means none do.

total.description: Every version there has ever been, however many are in `versions`.

oneOf.description:
How its agent was installed and the channel it follows. A package
install updates only to builds its own repository's channel holds.
Absent: an agent too old to say.

agent_mode.description:
⚠️ A **ceiling**, not a setting. The host's own `agent.toml` decides
this; the server may narrow it and can never widen it. A portal that
renders it as editable is describing a control that does not exist.

oneOf.description:
Its package sources are pinned in time (DAWG-233): `updates` is
measured against a snapshot that does not move. ⚠️ Zero updates on a
frozen host is **not** "patched", least of all when `behind`.

labels.description:
⚠️ A **selector**, not decoration. A policy that targets several labels
intersects them, and the fleet filter takes them as repeatable
`key=value`, so a client that cannot see the type cannot build either.
String to string, enforced by `hosts_labels_are_strings` rather than
asserted here (DAWG-261).

machine_id.description: Identity, and not the hostname. Hostnames change and repeat.

reboot_required.description:
⚠️ Three-valued. `null` is "this host cannot say", which is **not**
`false`. A distribution with no way to answer must not read as "nothing
to do here".

oneOf.description:
Whether this host can take snapshots, and so be rolled back
(DAWG-115). ⚠️ `null` is an agent too old to say, **not** a host that
cannot: that one has a `reason` and no `provider`.

⚠️ `null` means **never evaluated**, not zero. A host that has never
uploaded an inventory has never been looked at, and rendering that as
"0 updates" tells somebody their unevaluated fleet is fully patched.

advisory_coverage.description:
Whether anything rates this host's updates (DAWG-215):

- `covered`: advisories are published for its release.
- `no_feed`: its release is known and no advisory feed covers it — a
  derivative like Linux Mint, Pop!_OS or Raspbian. ⚠️ Every update
  here is unrated, which is not the same as safe.
- `unknown_release`: not resolved to a known release yet.

oneOf.description:
What the host said about the cloud it runs in, or absent because it is
not in one.

held_packages.description:
⚠️ An update for a held package will not install. This is the answer to
"why did nothing happen" before anybody has to ask it.

notes.description: Free text for whoever looks after the box.

proposals.description:
Open proposals only, newest first. A host that has been in four hundred
merged proposals is the normal case, and listing them would make this a
changelog rather than an answer to "is anything waiting on this box".

data.description:
What the event recorded. A job's events carry `job` (`job_…`); a
finished one also `status`, `changes` and `error`.

kind.description:
`job_finished`, `rejected_by_host`, `job_expired`, `went_stale`,
`recovered` — or something newer, passed through as stored.

next.description: Pass as `?after=` for the next page. Absent at the end. Opaque.

resolved_hosts.description:
Every host it resolves to, static or by label, each counted once.
Decommissioned hosts are in no group.

static_hosts.description: Hosts put in the group by hand. Decommissioned hosts are not counted.

changes.description: What the host reported changed. Empty until it reports.

error.description: The host's error, when it ran the job and it failed.

kind.description:
`apply_updates`, `reboot`, … or `unknown` for a document this build
cannot read.

pinned.description:
The exact versions the job was signed to install. Empty for a kind
that installs nothing named.

rejection_reason.description:
Why the host refused it, when it did. A refusal is normal: the host's
own configuration always wins.

report_unreadable.description:
There is a report and this build cannot read it. Never true alongside
any of the fields above.

retried_at.description:
Set when a person resumed past this job's failure, and its host was
sent a new job, which is listed too (DAWG-110).

status.description:
`queued`, `delivered`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`,
`rejected_by_host`, `cancelled` or `expired`. Anything else is passed
through as stored.

name.description: The person's name, as their colleagues will see it.

median_hours.description: Hours from a fix being available to it being installed.

resolved.description: Exposures to this severity that ended in the period.

severity.description:
`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low` or `none`; absent for advisories
nobody rated.

target_days.description:
The organization's target for this severity; absent for `none` and
unrated.

within_target.description: How many of `resolved` were within the target.

finished.description:
The job has finished. With `more` false, nothing further will arrive —
bar a last batch that is still in flight, for a few seconds.

more.description: Ask again with `after` = the last line's `seq` for what follows.

csrf_token.description:
The token every mutation has to echo in `X-Updawg-Csrf`.

Returned here as well as at sign-in, so a page that has been reloaded
can get one without signing in again. It is safe to put in this body and
not in a cookie: a cross-origin page cannot read a response, and a
cookie would travel on every request whether it was wanted or not.

memberships.description: Organizations this person belongs to, and what they may do in each.

agent_auto_update.description: Whether agents are kept on the stable channel automatically (DAWG-46).

audit_retention_days.description:
Days the audit log is kept if fewer than the plan keeps, or `null` for
the plan's whole window (DAWG-160).

audit_retention_max_days.description: The most `audit_retention_days` may be on this plan.

eol_lead_days.description:
Days before a release's support ends to raise `release.eol`, longest
first (DAWG-70). 180, 90 and 30 unless somebody changed them.

role.description:
The caller's role, on every representation of an organization.

The portal needs it to decide what to render, and fetching it from
`GET /me` instead would mean the two can disagree after somebody's role
changes in another tab.

stale_after_minutes.description:
Minutes without a check-in before a host is marked stale (DAWG-62).
5 to 10,080; 30 unless somebody changed it.

name.description: Absent if the policy has since been hard-deleted.

version.description:
The version this proposal was generated under, which is very possibly
not the current one. That is the point of storing it.

fixable_since.description: When an update reaching the fix became available.

critical.description: Days to patch a fixable critical exposure. 1 to 365.

PlanBody.description: An unfinished release upgrade, and where its hosts stand.

oneOf.description: The group it was planned for. Absent for every host on the release.

hosts.description: Hosts it targets that are still in the fleet.

preflight.description: How many hosts stand where after their current preflight.

stuck.description:
Each host a check failed on, or that finished without answering, and
why.

from.description: The release its hosts run now: `13`.

group_id.description: Only the hosts in this group (`grp_…`). Absent is every host on `from`.

to.description: The release to move them to: `14`. One of `from`'s `targets`.

PolicyProblem.description: One thing wrong with a policy, where an editor can put a marker.

detail.description:
The path serde walked, then what went wrong: `rules[0]: unknown field
...`. The location is **not** repeated here — it is `line` and `column`.

line.description:
One-based, as an editor counts. Absent for the two checks that need the
whole document and so have no line of their own: a rule naming a
rollout the policy does not define, and `apply: asap_in_window` with no
window. Both name the rule by index in `detail` instead.

yaml.description:
`Option` so that a missing field produces this API's own 400 rather
than axum's plain-text 422 — see DAWG-246 and the note in
`routes::proposals::reject`.

blocked.description: Why one cannot be asked for now. Absent when it can.

hosts.description: Every host the proposal targets that is still in the fleet.

oneOf.description: Who asked last, and when. Absent until somebody does.

items.description: The specifics: a package, a file, a module.

name.description:
Stable, for code: `disk_space`, `held_packages`, `modified_conffiles`,
`dkms_modules`, `snapshot`, `reboot`, for a package change
`approved_only`, and for a release upgrade `release_upgrade` and
`third_party_repos`. A newer agent may add more.

summary.description: One sentence for a person, saying what to do when it is not a pass.

checks.description:
What the host found, once it has reported. A failing check is an
answer, not a failed job.

job_status.description:
The current preflight job's status: `queued`, `delivered`, `running`,
`succeeded`, `failed`, `rejected_by_host`, `expired`, `cancelled`.
Absent before one is signed for this host.

problem.description:
Why there are no checks: the host refused the job (an agent not
permitted `preflight` says so), or it failed.

Preview.description: The difference between two policy sets, over one fleet.

changing.description:
Same key before and after, and something about it differs: more hosts,
more packages, a worse severity — or, the one that matters,
[`Action::AutoMerge`] where it used to be [`Action::Propose`]. Carries
the **after** shape.

⚠️ This list exists because of a bug I wrote and then tested for.
`unchanged` originally held every shared key, so turning `propose` into
`auto_merge` — which opens no proposal, closes none and loses no
coverage — made [`Preview::is_empty`] report a no-op. A portal using
that to decide whether to warn would have stayed silent for the single
most dangerous edit anybody can make to a policy.

closing.description: Proposals that exist now and would not.

dropped.description:
⚠️ Updates a rule decides today and nothing would decide after.

The half that does not show up in proposal counts, and the one that
leaves a fleet unpatched. An `ignore` rule counts as deciding: choosing
to do nothing is not the same as nothing matching.

newly_covered.description: Updates nothing decides today and a rule would decide after.

opening.description: Proposals that do not exist now and would.

changes_nothing.description: Whether saving this would change anything at all.

complete.description:
⚠️ `false` means the fleet was larger than one preview evaluates, so
host counts are lower bounds. Which *kinds* of proposal appear is still
reliable — those come from the rules rather than from the hosts.

hosts_evaluated.description: How many hosts this answer is about.

would_auto_merge.description: How many proposals would go out with nobody looking at them, after this.

replaces.description:
The policy this document would replace, as `pol_<hex>`. Absent means a
policy that does not exist yet — see [`preview`].

changes.description:
What changes, grouped by package and by the versions involved — **not**
one entry per host per package, which on a real fleet is tens of
thousands of them. See `db::inbox`.

reboot.description:
What approving this lets it do about reboots (DAWG-103), as the rule
said when the proposal was opened: `never`, `immediate` (reboot hosts
that need it as part of the job) or `in_window` (the same, only inside
the maintenance window). An agent reboots only if its own agent.toml
permits it.

oneOf.description:
A release upgrade's from and to (`kind` `dist_upgrade`, DAWG-153).
Absent on a package change, which says what it changes in `changes`.

targets.description:
⚠️ **`targets`, not `hosts`.** This struct flattens [`SummaryBody`],
which already has a `hosts` — a count. Naming the list `hosts` too made
the array silently shadow the number, so the same key was an integer on
the list endpoint and an array on this one. Nothing failed: `serde`
flattening has a last-one-wins rule and is happy to apply it. A
generated client cannot express that, and a portal reading
`proposal.hosts` would get whichever it was last given.

Found by running `scripts/try-proposals.sh` and reading the output,
which is the only place a key that collides with itself is visible.

targets_complete.description:
Whether `targets` is all of them. The *count* in `hosts` is always
exact; this list is capped.

next.description:
Pass as `?after=` for the next page. Absent at the end, so a client
stops rather than asking for a page it has been told is empty.

total.description: How many match the filter, not how many are in this page.

ProposalState.description:
The body every one of the three answers with.

Named for what it is rather than for the endpoint, because all three return
it and a portal that has just clicked a button wants the same three facts
whichever button it was: where the proposal is now, and how the approval
count stands.

approvals.description:
Distinct people who have approved. A rejected proposal keeps the count
it had: it is a record of who had agreed before somebody said no.

outstanding.description:
How many more approvals this needs before it can go ahead.

Zero once there are enough, and zero once there is nothing left to go
ahead with — see [`ok`].

required.description: What the policy asked for, via `proposals.required_approvals`.

scheduled_for.description:
When a proposal that is `scheduled` may start (DAWG-92).

Present only on that status, and omitted rather than null everywhere
else: it is not "unknown", it is "does not apply", and a portal that
renders a date field will render something for a null.

Proposed.description: One proposal, as the fleet would produce it.

action.description:
What would happen. `auto_merge` here is the answer to "would this go out
without anybody looking", which is the question a preview is really for.

hosts.description: How many hosts would be in it.

packages.description: How many distinct packages, across every host.

rollout.description: The named rollout strategy, if the rule named one the policy defines.

rule_index.description:
Which rule decided it, by position. Renders as "rule 3 of
web-production" — and is the reason reordering churns keys.

same_work_as.description:
Set on an **opening** entry when a **closing** one covers exactly the
same work under a different key, and the other way round. Almost always
a rule that moved. See the module documentation.

settings.description:
What else the rule decided. See [`Settings`] for why this is a struct
rather than the one field that used to be here.

providers.description:
The external sign-in providers this deployment has credentials for:
`github`, `google`, `microsoft`. The sign-in page shows a button each.

ReadinessBody.description: One third-party repository against one release the host could move to.

status.description:
`published`, `missing`, `unknown` (see `detail`) or
`not_release_specific` (the suite names no release and carries over).

target_suite.description: The suite that release would need: `cloud-sdk-forky`.

url.description: Where it is, as the agent sent it (credentials stripped on the host).

Reboot.description: What to do about a host that needs a reboot afterwards.

reason.description:
`Option` so that a missing field reaches `Reason::parse` rather than
axum's body rejection — see the note in [`reject`]. It is still
required; what is optional is which of the three ways of not sending it
the caller chose.

eol_active.description:
End of ordinary vendor support, where a community or paid tier
follows it.

hosts.description: Hosts in the fleet running it.

plans.description: Release upgrades from it that have not finished, newest first.

targets.description: Releases it can be upgraded to, oldest first.

unresolved_hosts.description: Hosts not resolved to a known release yet. No plan can name them.

delivery_id.description: The new delivery. The one replayed keeps its own record.

Requirement.description: A step that may be required before a proposal applies.

retrying.description: Hosts whose failed job will be signed again.

group.description: A value of the groups claim, exactly.

blocked.description:
Why one cannot be asked for now. Absent when it can, or when it has
been.

hosts.description:
The hosts it restores, each to the snapshot it took before this
proposal changed it.

oneOf.description: Who asked, and when. Absent until somebody does.

skipped.description: Hosts the proposal changed that it cannot restore, and why.

job_status.description:
The rollback job's status once it is signed: `queued`, `delivered`,
`running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `rejected_by_host`, `expired`.

job.description: Its current job's status, or null before it has one.

oneOf.description: When the rollout stops itself. Null when there is no rollout.

halt_reason.description: Why it halted, in words, when it did.

stages.description: In order. A stage may have no hosts: a canary stage with no canaries.

status.description: Null until it starts; then running, soaking, halted, completed or cancelled.

strategy.description: The rollout's name in the policy, or null for every host at once.

RolloutSummaryBody.description: One rollout, for the Rollouts page.

current_stage.description: The stage it is in, or stopped in.

failed.description: Hosts whose current job failed, was refused or expired.

proposal_id.description: The `prp_…` id of the proposal it carries out.

staged.description:
In stages, by a strategy the rule named. `false`: every host at once,
one stage with no name.

status.description: Running, soaking, halted, completed or cancelled.

strategy.description: The rollout's name in the policy; empty for one that is not staged.

from.description:
The `sk_…` the caller believes is active. When given and no longer
true, the answer is `409` and nothing is queued — a page that is a
rotation out of date must not rotate a key its reader never saw.

signing_secret.description: `whsec_…`. See the webhook signing scheme in the API docs.

SavedChannelBody.description:
A channel just saved, and — for a webhook whose configuration was just set
— the secret its requests are signed with. ⚠️ **Shown once**: it is
stored encrypted with the rest of the configuration and never returned
again. Replace the configuration to get a new one.

base_url.description: Where the provider sends SCIM requests.

issued.description: Whether a token has been issued.

token.description: `scim_…`. Shown once; only its hash is kept.

hosts.description:
Every static member, as `hst_…` ids. Replaces the set; label-selected
members are unaffected.

Settings.description:
Everything a rule decides about a proposal other than which updates are in
it.

⚠️ This exists because running the endpoint found a hole. `action` was the
only rule-derived field compared, so raising `min_approvers` from one to two
— which is somebody deciding this change needs a second person — came back
as `changes_nothing: true`. So did requiring a snapshot, or moving a
proposal onto a different rollout.

The fields here are the ones a rule sets and a person would want to be asked
about. `earliest_apply_at` is deliberately **not** among them: it is
computed from the clock and the maintenance window, so it differs between
two runs of the same unchanged policy, and a preview that reported a change
every time you looked at it is a preview nobody reads.

Severity.description:
How bad an advisory is, on one scale.

# `Severity::None` is not the same as no severity

This enum is what a vendor *said*. Somewhere it is stored as a nullable
column and read back as `Option<Severity>`, and the two levels mean
different things:

- `None` (the variant) — rated, and rated as not worth acting on. Ubuntu's
  `negligible` and Debian's `unimportant` land here.
- `Option::None` — **nobody rated it.** Debian DSAs frequently carry no
  rating at all.

Collapsing them would let a policy written `severity >= low` quietly skip
everything nobody had got round to rating yet, which is the opposite of what
somebody writing that rule wants.

name.description: The person's name, as their colleagues will see it.

organization.description:
The organization's name. Its slug is derived from it, and can be
changed later in Settings.

csrf_token.description: The token every mutation echoes in `X-Updawg-Csrf`.

SigningKeyBody.description: A key as the list shows it. Public halves only; there is no other kind here.

customer_held.description:
The organization holds this key and signs in its own environment.
Updawg cannot sign with it, and cannot rotate it.

endorsed_by.description: The `sk_…` that endorsed this one. Absent on an organization's first.

public_key.description: `ed25519:` and the SPKI DER in base64 — the form an agent pins.

provider.description:
The provider in use, e.g. `snapper`. Absent: none, and `reason` says
why.

until.description: RFC 3339, as every other timestamp this API takes or gives.

oneOf.description: Absent until one is saved.

redirect_uri.description: What to register at the provider as the sign-in redirect URI.

default_role.description: For somebody no mapping matches; absent refuses them.

client_secret.description: Required the first time; absent afterwards keeps the stored one.

issuer.description:
The provider's issuer, exactly as its discovery document names it:
`https://acme.okta.com`, `https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0`,
`https://accounts.google.com`.

enforced.description: Whether it must: no emailed link, no GitHub.

sso.description: Whether this address signs in through its organization's provider.

start_url.description: Where to send the browser to do that.

txt_name.description: The TXT record to publish: its name…

domain.description:
`example.com`. Addresses at it, and only it, sign in through the
connection once it is verified.

soak_seconds.description: How long to wait after this stage before the next. Null for none.

soak_until.description: When its soak ends, while it soaks.

status.description: Null until the rollout starts; then pending, running, soaking, completed, halted or cancelled.

StandingBody.description: Hosts by where their current preflight leaves them.

no_answer.description: Finished without checks: refused by the agent, failed or expired.

not_run.description: No preflight signed for it yet.

cancelled.description: Jobs cancelled before any host had them.

still_out.description:
Jobs a host already holds. Not cancelled: they finish and report as
normal, because an agent that holds a verified job runs it.

version.description:
Which version is in force. Named `version` rather than
`current_version` because from outside there is only one that matters,
and `?version=` takes this same number.

known_exploited.description:
Something it fixes is on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list
(DAWG-72). Shown beside the severity; it never raises it.

max_severity.description:
`null` means nothing in this proposal was rated, which is **not** the
same as harmless.

outstanding.description:
Zero for anything final, whatever the counts say — see
[`db::inbox::Summary::outstanding`].

status.description:
A status this build does not recognise is passed through as stored
rather than hidden or guessed at. A portal should render an unknown
status as unknown — it means this API is older than the thing that wrote
the row, which is a deployment fact worth seeing.

TestResultBody.description:
How a test send went. A channel that did not accept the message is an
answer, not an error: the request to try worked.

error.description:
Why not, in the other side's words where there were any. Never the
destination.

total.description: Every comment on the proposal, including any outside this page.

TokenBody.description: A token as a list shows it: everything but the value.

usable.description:
Whether an agent presenting it now would be let in: not revoked, not
expired, not used up. The same three conditions the gateway checks, so
the portal does not have to know them.

uses.description:
Hosts that enrolled with it **and then checked in**. A use is charged on
the first check-in, not when the certificate is issued, so an attempt the
agent refused costs nothing (DAWG-224).

fixed_upstream.description: The version that fixes it in Debian unstable. Absent: fixed nowhere.

package.description:
The source package the security tracker names — or, when `binary`, a
binary one.

urgency.description:
`low`, `medium` or `high`. ⚠️ Absent means nobody rated it, not that
it is harmless.

vulnerability.description: `CVE-…`, or the tracker's `TEMP-…` for one without a CVE yet.

config.description:
A whole new configuration for the channel's kind, replacing the old
one. There is no merging into what is stored: nothing can read it back
to merge into.

UpdateGroupRequest.description:
Every field optional. An absent field is left alone; `null` clears
`description` or `label_selector`.

UpdateHostRequest.description:
Every field optional. An absent field is left alone; `null` clears
`display_name` or `notes`. `labels` replaces the whole set.

labels.description:
⚠️ The **whole** set, not a merge. A merge could never remove a label,
and a label is a selector: one left behind keeps the host in a group.

UpdateKind.description:
`Ord` is derived so this can key an ordered collection — the policy engine
groups proposals by kind in a `BTreeMap` and needs a total order to produce
the same output twice. The order itself is the declaration order and carries
no meaning; nothing should read severity into it.

agent_auto_update.description:
Keep agents on the stable channel without anybody approving each
update (DAWG-46). When stable moves, an agent update is opened and
approved on your authority, for every host behind it whose agent.toml
permits `self_update`. It stays yours: if you stop administering the
organization, nothing more is signed until somebody turns it on again.

audit_retention_days.description:
Days to keep the audit log, 7 up to what the plan keeps
(`audit_retention_max_days`), or `null` for the plan's whole window
(DAWG-160). Owner only. Shortening it deletes the older entries at the
next nightly run, and nothing brings them back.

eol_lead_days.description:
Days before a release's support ends to raise `release.eol`, each 1
to 730, at most six (DAWG-70). Stored longest first without repeats.
Empty leaves only the alert when support has ended.

name.description: Absent means "leave it alone", which is not the same as an empty string.

stale_after_minutes.description:
Minutes without a check-in before a host is marked stale, 5 to 10,080
(DAWG-62). Set it above your longest expected outage — a reboot, a
maintenance window — or every one of them marks hosts stale.

policies_naming_old_name.description:
Live policies whose selector named the group's **old** name, and so now
match nothing of it. A policy selects a group by name. Empty unless the
name changed.

requiring_reboot.description:
Updates that will leave the host needing a reboot — distinct from
`reboot_required`, which is whether it needs one now.

days.description:
Every day with a recorded count, oldest first. A day nothing checked
in on has no row and costs nothing.

estimate_pence.description:
`host_days` on this plan's list price, in pence, for an organization
with a live subscription. An estimate: Stripe's invoice is the bill.

from.description: The first and last day of the month asked about.

host_days.description: The sum of `days`: what the month has used so far.

today_so_far.description:
Hosts that have checked in today so far, not yet in `days`. Only for
the current month.

active_hosts.description: Hosts that checked in during the day, UTC: the day's billable count.

errors.description:
⚠️ **At most one today.** serde stops at the first thing it cannot read,
so there is no second error to report — collecting them all needs a
parser that keeps going, which this one does not. An array rather than a
single object so that the shape does not have to change when it can.

name.description:
What the document says it is, when it is anything. Absent rather than
null-and-empty on a failure, because a half-populated body invites a
client to read fields that mean nothing.

WindowBody.description: A maintenance window, as a policy's compiled form has one.
